Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by the pound sign. There will be an instruction following the announcement. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; Dr. Lena Torres, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Kim Nguyen, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Reflecting on Q2, we are proud of the significant strides Voltara Motors has made across all facets of our business. We have achieved remarkable progress in delivery volumes by model and geographic region, average selling price trends by model and region, electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains, our strategic outlook and priorities for the next quarter and year ahead, revenue from software and services like subscriptions and autonomous driving features, total revenue and year-over-year growth, battery costs per kWh and downward trends, and the impact of our pricing strategies and promotional activities. The market reception to our CyberVolt pickup has been overwhelmingly positive, with the associated surge in fleet orders and premium variant uptake far exceeding our initial estimates.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in greater detail.

Marcus Hale:  
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. Our revenue for Q2 reached $14.2 billion, marking an exceptional 25% increase compared to the same period last year. Breaking this down further, this total revenue figure underscores the strength of our execution in a dynamic EV landscape. Automotive revenues, including vehicle sales, regulatory credits, and leasing, hit $11.9 billion, up 28% year-over-year, propelled by record deliveries and a stable average selling price. Regulatory credits contributed $450 million, up significantly as we monetized excess ZEV and CO2 compliance at premium rates. Our high-margin energy generation and storage segment added $1.5 billion, surging 45% from hyperscaler deals and residential Powerwall ramps under IRA incentives. Services and other revenues reached $350 million, up 20%, from Supercharger expansion and telematics subscriptions.

Gross margin expanded to 24%, driven by enhanced operational efficiencies, a favorable product mix shift toward high-margin SUVs and trucks, and battery cost reductions. Operating expenses amounted to $2.1 billion, reflecting scaled R&D investments in autonomy and next-gen cells, resulting in a net income of $850 million. Our financial position remains strong, with $8.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We anticipate $15 to $16 billion in revenue for the upcoming quarter.

Diving deeper into deliveries, our north star metric, we achieved record quarterly deliveries of 248,700 vehicles in Q2, up 28% year-over-year from 194,200 and 12% quarter-over-quarter from Q1's 221,900. This is our 10th straight quarter of growth, powered by Shanghai Giga Factory's full run-rate on Model Y Long Range and robust U.S. CyberVolt demand ahead of IRA credit changes. H1 totals 470,600, on pace for 1.05 to 1.1 million full-year, barring macro shocks like high interest rates.

Model mix shifted to high-margin SUVs and trucks at 78% of volume, up from 65% last year, as sedans face legacy OEM pressure like Ford's Mustang Mach-E. Model Y, our crossover SUV leader, delivered 142,300 units or 57% of total, up 35% YoY and 15% QoQ, thanks to HW4 autonomy stack launch enabling Level 3 FSD Supervised, boosting conversions 22%. ASP held at $48,500 with 48% FSD attach at $12,000. Fremont and Shanghai averaged 1,550 per week, 4680 cells cutting COGS 8% QoQ.

CyberVolt pickup surged to 62,400 units, 25% mix, up 52% YoY from Texas GigaTex ramp to 800 weekly, outperforming Cybertruck estimates and grabbing 18% U.S. pickup share. Steer-by-wire and 800V architecture enable 350 kW charging to 80% in 18 minutes, drawing fleets like Amazon at 15% of orders. ASP $72,800, 35% Tri-Motor Plaid.

Model S/X combined 32,100 units, 13% mix, flat YoY but up 8% QoQ post-refresh: S at 12,400 units, $95,000 ASP; X 19,700, $102,000. Plaid drove 62% premium upsells, 28% margins vs. 22% fleet-wide.

Model 3 at 11,900 units, 5% mix, down 15% YoY from Highland delays and BYD Seagull pressure; idling lines for CyberVolt but H2 rebound via European LFP.

Geographically, North America at 112,400 or 45%, up 32%, led by 105,000 U.S. CyberVolt at 55,000; IRA cushions 2025 expiry. Europe 58,200, 23%, up 25%, Model Y 42,000 on German subsidies, Berlin ramp to 5,000 weekly, 12% share. China 52,100, 21%, up 18%, Shanghai 1,200 weekly despite BYD volume; Model Y RWD captured 8% premium SUV. APAC ex-China 19,500, 8%, up 45% on Australia RHD and Japan pilots. Rest of World 6,500, 3%, up 50% via Mexico/Brazil CKD and UAE fleets.

Our 72% SUV/truck mix balances portfolio vs. sedans' ASP erosion. Panasonic 4680 yields at 92% enabled 98% on-time deliveries. Challenges like China NEV cuts pressured ASP 3%, but H2 catalysts include CyberVolt India, FSD v12.5 for $1.2 billion annualized software run-rate, Texas Phase 2 for compact SUV.

On ASP trends, blended at $54,200, up 7% YoY and 3% QoQ from $52,600. Eighth straight YoY growth from 62% truck/SUV mix, up from 55%, and 28% FAS attach adding $11,500 per vehicle. Premium packs with 800V and LFP-NCM hybrids boosted density 10%.

By model: Apex S luxury sedan $76,800 ASP, up 5% on 45% Plaid sales with Track Pack. Apex Y $49,500, flat YoY up 2% QoQ, bundling free Supercharging, 38% AWD Performance. Apex T pickup $73,200, up 12% on Adventure packages, 15,000 units doubling YoY. Apex 2 entry $33,400, down 3% ramping to 200,000 annual, 65% margins.

Regions: North America $58,700, up 10%, 70% truck mix, 35% FAS. Europe $51,200, up 2%, CO2 tailwinds. China $42,800, down 1% pricing war but OTA adds $5,000. APAC $47,900, up 6% RHD growth. North America drives 28% margins; China dual-brand stabilizes.

Software and services generated $1.82 billion, up 162% YoY and 28% QoQ, 7.2% of total revenue. Subscriptions $1.12 billion at 48% attach, $14.50 ARPU tiered $9.99-$19.99. Autonomy $450 million, 18% HW4.0 penetration, 2.5 million disengagement-free miles. Ancillaries $250 million from cloud data and OTA packs. 89% margins via ApexForge supercomputer.

North America $920 million, China $520 million NOP+, Europe $280 million GDPR tweaks. ARPU compounding 25%, Q3 guide $2.3 billion with FVA Unsupervised.

Battery costs at $98/kWh pack, $85 cell, down 17% YoY, below $115 industry. 19% CAGR past 24 months: $165 '21, $129 '22, $118 '23, $95 Q4 guide. CTP 2.0, silicon anodes, LFP 55%, recycling $75/kWh. China $62/kWh, NA $92 effective IRA, Europe $112. Guide $85 '25, $72 '27.

Pricing strategies held blended ASP $48,200, up 1.8% YoY adjusted. Premium Pro SUV $72,500 ATP, 65% autonomy take. Core sedan cut $2,500 to $39,900. Dynamic AI pricing, IRA net +12% NA. Promotions $4,200 average: 0% APR 42% uptake, $3,000 conquest cash 18,000 sales. Compressed margins 210 bps but EBITDA to 12.1%, inventory turns 4.2x.

Range improvements averaged 22% uplift to 428 miles fleet-wide, 2.4 mi/kWh efficiency, 118 MPGe. Apex 482 miles beating Model S. 46-series cells 850 Wh/L, SiC inverters 98% efficiency, Cd 0.23, OTA v2.4 +5%. NA 62% volume, Europe WLTP 680 km, China LFP dual-source.

These integrate into 24% margins, $82/kWh packs trending sub-$70.

Next, we'll hear from Dr. Lena Torres regarding the latest developments in our manufacturing operations.

Dr. Lena Torres:  
Thank you, Marcus. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at optimal levels to meet the surging demand for our vehicles. We have successfully implemented advanced automation technologies, including gigacasting and cell-to-pack integration at Fremont, Shanghai, Texas GigaTex, and Berlin, resulting in increased production output of over 10,000 vehicles weekly, reduced cycle times by 25%, and 92% utilization rates. Yields on 4680 cells hit 92%, enabling structural packs that cut weight and costs while ramping Spartanburg to 500,000 capacity in 2025.

Following me, Raj Patel will provide an update on our technological innovations.

Raj Patel:  
Thank you. Our R&D team is relentlessly pursuing breakthroughs in battery technology like silicon anodes and solid-state pilots targeting 1,000 Wh/L, autonomous driving systems with Apex Neural Net v2.0 logging millions of disengagement-free miles, and vehicle connectivity via 5G ApexLink. Range gains to 428 miles, 92% wheel-to-wheel efficiency from axial-flux motors and OTA optimizations position us to redefine mobility, with V2G unlocking ancillary revenue.

After me, Kim Nguyen will offer insights into our supply chain strategies.

Kim Nguyen:  
Thank you. We have established a resilient and diversified supply chain network, multi-sourcing lithium, nickel, cobalt via Piedmont and BHP offtakes hedging 70% exposure, reducing China reliance to 40% for U.S. models. This mitigated global challenges, achieving 98% on-time deliveries vs. peers' lower rates, with recycling JVs yielding low-cost recycled cathode and regional arbitrage keeping blended costs competitive.

Next, Jordan Lee will share updates on our sales performance and market expansion initiatives.

Jordan Lee:  
Thank you. Our sales team has achieved remarkable success in expanding our market reach and driving revenue growth. Strong demand across regions, with CyberVolt fleets and Model Y subsidies fueling 28% delivery growth. We're pursuing India launch, ASEAN pilots, and Europe ramp, maintaining 420,000 backlog through dynamic pricing and conquest promotions.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:  
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad followed by the pound sign. Our first question comes from Sarah Chen at Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:  
Thanks for taking my question. Can you provide more color on the delivery breakdown by model and region, and how that ties into your full-year guidance?

Elena Vasquez:  
Great question, Sarah. As Marcus detailed, Q2's 248,700 deliveries marked record growth, with Model Y at 57%, CyberVolt surging 52% YoY to 25% mix from Texas ramp. Geos: NA 45% up 32%, Europe 23% on subsidies, China 21% despite competition. This H1 pace supports 1.05-1.1 million FY, with H2 catalysts like FSD rollout and capacity adds.

Operator:  
Our next question from Mike Rodriguez at Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:  
Marcus, on ASP trends—how are you managing mix shifts and software upsells amid pricing pressures?

Marcus Hale:  
Mike, blended ASP $54,200 up 7% YoY from 62% premium mix and 28% FAS attach adding $11,500. Model-specific: T pickup $73,200 up 12%, Y stable at $49,500 via bundles. Regions show NA premium at $58,700, China resilient despite wars. Software like $199/month FVA drives recurring lift.

Operator:  
Next from Lisa Patel at JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:  
For manufacturing, what's the latest on gigafactory ramps and automation impacts on costs?

Dr. Lena Torres:  
Lisa, Fremont and Shanghai at 92% utilization post-automation, Texas GigaTex 800/week CyberVolt, Berlin 5,000/week. 4680 integration cut COGS 8%, structural packs shave $12/kWh, positioning Spartanburg for 500k capacity and sub-$70/kWh packs by 2026.

Operator:  
From David Kim at Barclays.

Analyst 4:  
Raj, details on range and efficiency gains—how do they compare competitively and factor into OTA?

Raj Patel:  
David, fleet 428 miles up 22% YoY, 2.4 mi/kWh via SiC 98% efficiency, Cd 0.23, OTA v2.4 +5% to 92% fleet. Beats Model S, tailored NA trucks 510 miles, Europe WLTP 680 km. V3.0 ML profiles target another 4-6%, correlating to 7% delivery uplift.

Operator:  
From Emma Walsh at Deutsche Bank.

Analyst 5:  
Supply chain outlook—how are you hedging battery materials amid volatility?

Kim Nguyen:  
Emma, 70% offtakes with Piedmont/BHP hedge 25% volatility, recycling 92% recovery at $75/kWh. Multi-hub: China LFP $62, NA IRA-effective $92, Europe Northvolt $105. Diversification de-risks, supports $85/kWh '25 guide.

Operator:  
From Tom Nguyen at Citi.

Analyst 6:  
Jordan, sales strategy on pricing and promos—impact on backlog and share gains?

Jordan Lee:  
Tom, disciplined ASP via dynamic AI, $4,200 incentives drove 35% Q3 volume, 0% APR 42% uptake, conquest $3,000 for 18k sales. Backlog 420k units, 1.2 pts NA share to 14.8%, TCO leadership vs. Tesla.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Operator:  
From Rachel Lee at RBC Capital.

Analyst 7:  
Elena, strategic priorities for H2 and 2025—production, innovation, expansion?

Elena Vasquez:  
Rachel, four pillars: scale Fremont/Spartanburg to 250k '25 deliveries 90-115% growth; innovate with 800V Apex Plus Q4, Orion $45k mid-'25, solid-state JV; expand Europe/China 25% mix; efficiency to FCF positive, $650-800M '25 EBITDA on $15.5B rev. Capex $1.2B focused batteries.

Operator:  
Final question from Alex Ford at Piper Sandler.

Analyst 8:  
Marcus, on software revenue trajectory and battery cost trends?

Marcus Hale:  
Alex, software $1.82B Q2, 162% YoY, 48% attach $14.50 ARPU, 89% margins; Q3 $2.3B with Robotaxi. Batteries $98/kWh down 17%, silicon/CTB/dry electrode to $85 '25, recycling key. Flows $1,500 FCF/vehicle.

Operator:  
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering exceptional results and creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q2 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
